::: {.lead}
In Lectures 2 and 3 you learned the parts of a computer, the GPU and video
memory, and how settings change the frame rate. Today you compare devices
with the requirements of a game. There are no new ideas: two short
problems. Do each one alone. The results of the activities are at the end
of this worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- The **GPU** draws the pixels. An integrated GPU shares the RAM; a
  graphics card has its own video memory (VRAM).
- 1080p has about twice the pixels of 720p: about half the frame rate.
- Higher textures need more video memory; shadows lower the frame rate.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the CPU|240 fps"}
Which part colours the pixels of a frame?
:   the GPU

A game runs at 120 fps at 720p. About how fast at 1080p?
:   about 60 fps

Where does an integrated GPU keep its textures?
:   in the main RAM
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Does Neon Drift run here?

A store page lists the **system requirements** of a game. **Minimum:** the
game runs at low settings. **Recommended:** it runs well. Compare each line
with the same line of the spec sheet. **The weakest line decides** the
level of the whole device.

*Neon Drift* for PC: minimum 4 cores at 2.5 GHz, 8 GB RAM, 2 GB video
memory, 20 GB free; recommended 6 cores at 3.5 GHz, 16 GB RAM, a graphics
card with 6 GB, 20 GB free on an SSD.

![Laptop L1 against the requirements.](images/compare-lines.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/spec-check.html" poster="sims/spec-check.png" title="Spec Check: does Neon Drift run here?" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · The lab computer · 15 min"}
1. In **Spec Check**, choose **My lab computer**. Enter its values (from
   Settings → System → About and Task Manager → Performance).
2. Write the level of the lab computer and its weakest line.

*Your product:* one level and one weakest line.

::: {.check}
Many lab computers reach the **minimum**: enough cores and RAM, but an
integrated GPU with about 2 GB, so the graphics line is the weakest. A lab
computer with a graphics card of 6 GB or more and 16 GB of RAM reaches the
recommended level.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The weakest line"}
Laptop L1: 8 cores, 4.4 GHz; 16 GB; GPU inside the processor, 2 GB; 120 GB
free, SSD. Old PC O1: 4 cores, 3.0 GHz; 4 GB RAM; graphics card, 2 GB;
60 GB free. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the processor|recommended"}
Which line holds Laptop L1 back?
:   graphics

Which level does Old PC O1 reach?
:   below minimum

A PC meets only the minimum. How does the game run?
:   at low settings
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Compatibility or performance?

A **compatibility problem** stops the game from installing or starting:
the OS is too old, or the free storage is too small. More power does not
help. A **performance problem** makes the game slow. The weakest part is
the **bottleneck**: when it is the GPU, lower the resolution and the
shadows.

![Compatibility problem and performance problem.](images/two-problems.png){width=86%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Your phone · 15 min"}
1. Open the store page of a game you play. **Android:** About this game →
   Requires Android. **iPhone:** Information → Compatibility. Write the OS
   version it needs and its size. Compare them with your phone.
2. A friend's phone runs the game at 25 fps, and the GPU is the
   bottleneck. Write two settings to lower.

*Your product:* a comparison with numbers, and two settings.

::: {.check}
A good answer: "Requires Android 8.0 and up, 180 MB. My phone has Android
13 and 12 GB free, so there is no compatibility problem." The settings:
lower the resolution (fewer pixels) and turn the shadows off. Both give the
GPU less work.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Which problem?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="buy more RAM"}
A phone has Android 9. The game needs Android 10.
:   a compatibility problem

The game runs, but at 25 fps.
:   a performance problem

The GPU is the bottleneck. What helps first?
:   lower the resolution and the shadows

The phone has 3 GB free. The game needs 4 GB.
:   a compatibility problem
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. What is the difference between the minimum and the recommended requirements?
2. A laptop has every line at the recommended level, but only 6 GB of RAM (minimum 8 GB). Which level does it reach?
3. Is "the game needs Android 11, the phone has Android 10" a compatibility or a performance problem?
4. A game runs at 30 fps and the GPU is the bottleneck. Name one setting to lower.

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Minimum: the game runs at low settings. Recommended: it runs well.
2. Below the minimum: the weakest line decides.
3. A compatibility problem.
4. The resolution or the shadows.
:::
